simple.meaning: נָעַר (nâʻar) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to growl.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 1 time in Jeremiah, beginning at Jeremiah 51:38. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to נָעַר (H5286) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: נָעַר (nâʻar) / H5286 is traced through Jeremiah 51:38 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H5286. naar I. [ נָעַר ] verb growl (Late Hebrew id. cry, bray ; compare Syriac ; Arabic make a noise Lane 2815 ; possibly Assyrian na'ru , cry , roar (?) Dl HWB 439 ); — only Qal Perfect 3plural אֲרָיוֺת כְּגוֺרֵי נָָֽעֲרוּ Jer 51:38 (|| יִשְׁאָ֑גוּ כַּכְּפִרִים ).

occurrences.englishText: They will roar together like young lions.
